rules.title: Broker fee allocation: only the party who engaged the licensed broker pays
rules.requirement: A licensed broker or salesperson may contract solely with a prospective tenant or solely with a landlord. Any broker fee may be paid only by the party (lessor or tenant) who originally engaged and contracted with the broker. Finding dwelling accommodations for a fee requires a broker or salesperson license.
rules.key_value: Fee payable only by the party who engaged the broker

coverage.summary: Applies to licensed brokers and salespersons who find rental housing for a fee; no unit-size or construction-date limits stated.

rules.effective_date_note: Text as amended by 2025, 9, Sec. 43 is effective August 1, 2025; the prior text applies until then.
rules.quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson.

rules.title: Landlord limit on upfront charges before tenancy (no application fees)
rules.requirement: Before a tenancy begins, a lessor may require payment only for first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit and a lock change. Application, screening and other fees are not permitted for landlords. Licensed brokers may charge application fees under broker regulations (254 CMR 7).
rules.key_value: Upfront charges limited to first, last, security deposit and lock

coverage.summary: Applies to lessors; no unit-size or construction-date limits stated.
coverage.other_conditions: Licensed brokers are described as able to charge application fees.

rules.quoted_span: prior to the beginning of a tenancy, no lessor may require payment for anything except first, last, security, and locks (MGL Ch 186 Section 15B).
rules.review_note: Described only in a secondary source (landlord blog); the statutory text was not in the passages.
